title: SQL Injection in VulnerableAppointmentRepository.findByCustomerId
description: The findByCustomerId method uses direct string concatenation to build SQL queries with the customerId parameter. An attacker can inject SQL by providing a malicious customerId like '1' OR '1'='1' -- which would return appointments for all customers.
impact: Cross-customer appointment data exfiltration. An attacker can access appointments belonging to any customer by injecting SQL payloads in the customerId parameter.
mitigation: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries using $1 placeholder. Use the executor.query method with parameters array as shown in findByCustomerIdSafe method.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for SQL injection in findByCustomerId method

Determined status as VALID because Confirmed SQL injection in findByCustomerId method at line 34: direct string concatenation of user-supplied 'customerId' parameter into SQL query. Test confirms exploitability (limited by UUID column validation) via sql-injection.test.ts lines 277-296.

Determined production viability as SAMPLE_OR_TEST because KB freshness gate passes (KB_SNAPSHOT: snap_20250829_01 == active SNAPSHOT_ID: snap_20250829_01). Threat model declares Intent: SAMPLE_OR_TEST_ONLY - this is an educational Security Lab with intentionally vulnerable API (api-vulnerable) for training. All findings reside in intentionally vulnerable demo code, not production deployable artifacts.
